title: Fairness for Servicemembers and their Families Act of 2025
official_summary:
Fairness for Servicemembers and their Families Act of 2025

This act requires the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to periodically review and report on the maximum coverage available under the Servicemembers' Group Life Insurance and Veterans' Group Life Insurance programs. Specifically, the VA must review such coverage amount every five years, taking into account the average percentage by which the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U) increased in the five fiscal years preceding the review.

summary.headline: New law requires the VA to review the maximum life insurance coverage for servicemembers and veterans every five years.
summary.what_it_does: The Department of Veterans Affairs must review the top coverage amount offered under two life insurance programs: Servicemembers' Group Life Insurance and Veterans' Group Life Insurance. The review must happen every five years and consider how much consumer prices rose over the previous five fiscal years. The VA must report on what it finds. The summary does not say the law itself changes the coverage amounts.

who_it_affects.group: Servicemembers enrolled in Servicemembers' Group Life Insurance
who_it_affects.how: The maximum amount of their life insurance coverage will be reviewed every five years with rising prices in mind.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans enrolled in Veterans' Group Life Insurance
who_it_affects.how: The maximum amount of their life insurance coverage will be reviewed every five years with rising prices in mind.

who_it_affects.group: Families and beneficiaries of insured servicemembers and veterans
who_it_affects.how: The payouts they could receive are covered by the new regular review.
The agency must carry out the five-year reviews and report on the results.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 12, 2025; the summary does not give a specific start date for the first review.
